```{r setup, include = FALSE}
needs <- c("gdalraster", "vapour", "ximage")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.2,
  eval = all(vapply(needs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE))
)
```

rwarp warps rasters as gdalwarp does, in two steps you can look at. A
**plan** says which source pixels each part of the destination needs, and
reads nothing. The **warp** then runs on pixels you read however you like.

This page warps a small sea surface temperature raster onto Antarctic polar
stereographic, looks at the plan, and checks the result against gdalwarp.
It uses gdalraster to read, a file shipped with vapour, and ximage to plot.

```{r libraries, message = FALSE}
library(rwarp)
library(gdalraster)
```

## The source

`sst.tif` in vapour is sea surface temperature in kelvin south of Tasmania:
longitude 140 to 150 east, latitude 40 to 60 south, in pixels of 0.07
degrees.

```{r source}
f  <- system.file("extdata", "sst.tif", package = "vapour")
ds <- new(GDALRaster, f)
src_crs <- ds$getProjectionRef()
src_gt  <- ds$getGeoTransform()
src_dim <- c(ds$getRasterXSize(), ds$getRasterYSize())
src_dim
```

## The destination

A destination is a CRS, a geotransform and a size. Here it's polar
stereographic (EPSG:3031) at 10 km, over the source's bounding box, snapped
to whole kilometres:

```{r destination}
dst_crs <- "EPSG:3031"
res <- 10000
bb  <- transform_bounds(c(140, -60, 150, -40), "EPSG:4326", dst_crs)
ext <- c(floor(bb[1] / res), ceiling(bb[3] / res),
         floor(bb[2] / res), ceiling(bb[4] / res)) * res   # xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax
dst_dim <- as.integer(c(ext[2] - ext[1], ext[4] - ext[3]) / res)
dst_gt  <- c(ext[1], res, 0, ext[4], 0, -res)
dst_dim
```

## Plan

`warp_plan()` works out, from geometry alone, the window of the source each
chunk of the destination needs:

```{r plan}
plan <- warp_plan(src_crs, src_gt, src_dim, dst_crs, dst_gt,
                  dst_size = dst_dim, resample = "bilinear")
str(plan[[1]][[1]])
```

One chunk, reading the whole source. `fill_ratio` is low because the
destination is a rectangle in polar stereographic and the source a wedge in
it, so most of the area the destination maps onto in the source lies
outside the source. `scale_x` and `scale_y` are how far the bilinear kernel
widens: destination pixels are larger than source pixels here, and gdalwarp
widens its kernels when it downsamples.

## Warp

`warp_exec()` runs a plan, calling `read_fn` for each chunk's window.
gdalraster reads nodata as `NA`, and in double data rwarp treats `NaN` and
`NA` as nodata.

```{r warp}
read_fn <- function(xoff, yoff, xsize, ysize) {
  ds$read(1L, xoff, yoff, xsize, ysize, xsize, ysize)
}
sst <- warp_exec(plan, read_fn, src_crs, src_gt, dst_crs, dst_gt)
dim(sst)
```

The result is a matrix in R's orientation, row 1 at the top. The source, in
longitude and latitude, and the warp:

```{r plot-warp}
src <- matrix(read_fn(0, 0, src_dim[1], src_dim[2]), src_dim[2], byrow = TRUE)
pal <- hcl.colors(96, "RdYlBu", rev = TRUE)
zl  <- range(src, na.rm = TRUE) - 273.15
op  <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(2.5, 2.5, 2, 0.5))
ximage::ximage(src - 273.15, c(140, 150.01, -60.02, -40), zlim = zl, col = pal,
               asp = 1 / cos(50 * pi / 180), main = "sst.tif, longitude and latitude")
ximage::ximage(sst - 273.15, ext, zlim = zl, col = pal, asp = 1,
               main = "warped to EPSG:3031, 10 km")
par(op)
```

## Planning as gdalwarp does

gdalwarp would not warp this destination in one piece. Its rule splits a
chunk in two while the fill ratio is below 0.5 and the chunk is larger than
100 pixels. `warp_plan()` follows gdalwarp's rules when told how gdalwarp
sees the warp (see "Planning as gdalwarp does" in `?warp_plan`):

```{r plan-gdalwarp}
plan_g <- warp_plan(src_crs, src_gt, src_dim, dst_crs, dst_gt,
                    dst_size = dst_dim, resample = "bilinear",
                    nbands = 1L, working_type = "Float64", src_nodata = TRUE,
                    min_fill_ratio = 0.5, min_dst_size = 100L,
                    scale_origin = "output", split_antimeridian = FALSE)
chunks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(plan_g[[1]], as.data.frame))
chunks[c("dst_xoff", "dst_yoff", "dst_xsize", "dst_ysize", "src_xsize", "src_ysize", "fill_ratio")]
```

Each chunk reads only the source it needs:

```{r plot-chunks, fig.height = 5}
op <- par(mar = c(2.5, 2.5, 2, 0.5))
ximage::ximage(sst - 273.15, ext, zlim = zl, col = pal, asp = 1,
               main = "gdalwarp's chunks for this destination")
x0 <- dst_gt[1] + chunks$dst_xoff * res
y0 <- dst_gt[4] - chunks$dst_yoff * res
rect(x0, y0 - chunks$dst_ysize * res, x0 + chunks$dst_xsize * res, y0, border = "grey20")
text(x0 + chunks$dst_xsize * res / 2, y0 - chunks$dst_ysize * res / 2,
     sprintf("%.2f", chunks$fill_ratio), cex = 0.8)
par(op)
```

The numbers are each chunk's fill ratio. Chunks with no source at all are
left out of the plan, as gdalwarp skips them.

## The same as gdalwarp

gdalwarp, through `gdalraster::warp()`, onto the same grid. `-ot Float64`
and `-wt Float64` make it work and write in doubles, as rwarp does:

```{r gdalwarp}
sst_g <- warp_exec(plan_g, read_fn, src_crs, src_gt, dst_crs, dst_gt)

out <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
warp(f, out, t_srs = dst_crs, quiet = TRUE,
     cl_arg = c("-te", ext[c(1, 3, 2, 4)], "-ts", dst_dim, "-r", "bilinear",
                "-ot", "Float64", "-wt", "Float64"))
g  <- new(GDALRaster, out)
gd <- matrix(g$read(1L, 0, 0, dst_dim[1], dst_dim[2], dst_dim[1], dst_dim[2]),
             dst_dim[2], byrow = TRUE)
g$close()

identical(is.na(sst_g), is.na(gd))     # the same pixels have data
max(abs(sst_g - gd), na.rm = TRUE)     # and the same values, to rounding
```

The single-chunk plan reads the same pixels but differs a little, by up to
`r signif(max(abs(sst - gd), na.rm = TRUE), 2)` K here: each chunk
estimates its own kernel scale and approximates the transform along its own
rows, so how the destination is chunked shows in the values.

## Already have the pixels?

`warp_exec()` is a loop over the plan's chunks. When you already hold the
source pixels, `warp_buffer()` warps one window into one destination window,
the step `warp_exec()` runs for each chunk. Here the whole source, which is
what the one-chunk plan read:

```{r buffer}
v <- read_fn(0, 0, src_dim[1], src_dim[2])
sst_b <- warp_buffer(v, src_crs, src_gt, dst_crs, dst_gt, dst_size = dst_dim,
                     src_size = src_dim, resample = "bilinear")
identical(sst_b, sst)
```

```{r close, include = FALSE}
ds$close()
```

## Where next

- [Sentinel-2: two UTM zones onto one grid](https://hypertidy.github.io/rwarp/r/articles/sentinel2-warp.html):
  three bands from two tiles in different zones, mosaicked as gdalwarp
  mosaics them, the same as gdalwarp's to 1e-11.
- [GHRSST SST onto Antarctic polar stereographic](https://hypertidy.github.io/rwarp/r/articles/ghrsst-polar.html):
  a window of a global 0.01 degree COG, and the read function as the place
  to swap readers.
- `vignette("plan-inspect", package = "rwarp")`: what a plan holds, fill
  ratios, and tiling a large destination.
- `vignette("crs-strings", package = "rwarp")`: what PROJ makes of the
  strings you give it.
- [The rwarp book](https://hypertidy.github.io/rwarp/): the Rust crate
  underneath, and how its results compare with GDAL's.
